top.line: An analyst's blueprint for RiskMandate, the vendors already moving, and our answer: the controls fitted to the context.
top.para: Its thesis is grant against mandate; its CISO question is our credentials argument. Drata, Endor Labs, Socket, Sondera, AWS and gateways are moving in, which is good news: each has gravity around its tooling, and our remit runs across them. We provide the analysis and the controls each environment needs, with the policy open. Now we need use cases.

in-short.line: Seven lines: a blueprint, agreement, vendors moving, the architecture mapped, controls fitted to context, more players, customers.
in-short.para: An analyst suggested what to borrow from the summit's companies, and most of it fits. Drata and others are already in the space. Discover, evaluate, enforce and prove map onto our pieces. Our offer is the right control for each context. Their arrival is good news, since our remit runs across their tools. Now we need customers and use cases.

note.line: The note: seven companies to study, three to combine, a four-layer control plane, start small, and one CISO question.
note.para: A power user's note, written in a ChatGPT session: study seven companies as analogies, combine capability risk, machine-testable controls and data exposure, notice Drata and Endor moving in, build discover, evaluate, enforce and prove with the edge in dangerous sequences, start small, and ask CISOs which action they would never permit, even with valid credentials.

agree.line: Where we agree: the thesis is the behaviour policy, the question is our argument, and we already start small.
agree.para: Access against action is grant against mandate. Pellbridge's day had seven of nine incidents as legitimate calls with legitimate credentials. First customers name one agent, measure its grant and write its mandate. And the sequence of individually allowed actions is where checking one call at a time falls short.

landscape.line: Who is already there: Drata, Endor Labs, Socket, Bedrock Data, Sondera, AWS, gateways, testers and responders.
landscape.para: Drata's AI Agent Governance, 4 August 2026, compiles plain-English policy and enforces it inline through an MCP proxy, in limited availability for agents on Anthropic, with manual approval as an option. Endor governs coding agents; Socket's hook blocks risky packages; Sondera checks Cedar before each action; AWS evaluates at its gateway.

map.line: Their architecture, our pieces: the grant, the mandate and delta, hooks and compiled rules, and receipts.
map.para: Discover is the measured grant, the roadmap's understand stage; evaluate is the mandate and the delta; enforce is hooks that block in the agent's harness plus rules compiled to Cedar for gateways; prove is chained receipts and a replayable day. The roadmap adds risk acceptance and insurance, which the four layers leave out.

inline.line: Not another box in the middle: use hooks and the customers' own gateways, and be the policy they are compiled from.
inline.para: Intercepting tool calls ourselves puts a new dependency in line, lacks application context, and enters a full market. Hooks can block and keep session state for sequences, honestly labelled settings. The same rules in Cedar, kept by a gateway out of the agent's reach, become boundaries; so far shown on five rules against fourteen requests.

start.line: Where to start: hooks and existing gateways, the policy, sequences in hooks, and partners for skills and dependencies.
start.para: The analyst's P0 list, reordered: interception through hooks and the customer's gateways; behavioural policy, which we have; cross-step detection in stateful hooks; allow, block and approve generated from the policy; audit and replay, which we have; Socket and Endor Labs as partners. The policy layer, not another runtime layer.

customers.line: What we need now: three to five teams, one workflow and one agent each, to do this for real.
customers.para: The plan should work and the pieces exist. The analyst's question finds them: an action you would never permit, even with valid credentials, is the first row of a mandate. The customer programme starts with it, and how to help has six steps for anyone else.

limits.line: The note is paraphrased; vendor claims are theirs; our dots are rings; hooks are settings; the evidence is a demo; open code checked publicly.
limits.para: The note is AI-assisted, from a ChatGPT session. Capabilities and repositories were read on 21 October 2026, not tested. RiskMandate supplies policy for each layer, not a product in it. Hooks are kept by the agent's harness. Pellbridge is invented. Some companies may hold more code than we could see.

sources.line: An analyst's note, the vendors' own pages, and our related articles on the summit, roadmap, credentials and Cedar.
sources.para: The analyst's note of 21 October 2026, paraphrased; Drata's 4 August announcement; Endor Labs, Socket, Bedrock Data and Sondera's pages; AWS, Ping, Docker, Bishop Fox, Optiv, Kroll and Sygnia; and our briefing for the summit, the roadmap, the key is not the risk, commander's intent, Cedar and the policy vault, and our first customers.

fit.line: The controls fitted to the context: a prompt, a hook, a gateway, or monitoring and a person, depending on what is at stake.
fit.para: What we provide is a map of the whole situation: an understanding of each environment, a risk analysis of each agent, and the set of controls that fits. Most vendors sell one of those answers. The behaviour policy says which each row needs, so a rule can move from prompt to hook to gateway as the stakes rise.

players.line: More players is good news: the problem is real, and each vendor has gravity around its own tooling.
players.para: Drata around its trust platform, Socket around packages, a gateway around its gateway: natural, and also the limit. Our remit covers the whole set of agents, environments and controls, across whichever tools a customer runs. Even connecting those tools to one policy is valuable on its own.

open.line: Who plays open source: enforcement points often are; governance platforms mostly are not; we open the policy layer.
open.para: agentgateway, Docker's MCP gateway and Sondera's harness are open; AWS opens Cedar; Socket and Endor Labs open their agent tooling; no public code was found for Drata's, Bedrock Data's or Ping's agent products. We are not the only open ones; what we open is the policy, the analysis and the vocabulary that feed the gateways.

maturity.line: The more mature the company, the less of what we do it may need, and there is still a lot of value to add.
maturity.para: Mature companies have gateways, monitoring and governance already; we add the risk analysis across them, the gaps between tools, the rows nobody holds, and evidence for a board or insurer. Less mature companies start with us. The platform is mouldable: policies, hooks, vaults, compiled rules and replayable evidence. It needs use cases.
